title: ENU Biometric Stage - Rejection/Reason Codes (Code-Verified)
description: All rejection and reason codes for the enu-biometric service (BIO stage, substage BIO_DEDUP). Each code has been traced through the actual Java source to confirm: (1) whether it is actively thrown or dead (defined but never used), (2) the exact method and line that triggers it, (3) the condition that causes it, (4) what happens to the packet, (5) whether it is retryable, and (6) what a CRM agent should advise the resident.

Thrown as an ApplicationException when any unanticipated non-ApplicationException technical error occurs while processing an ABIS-MW inbound Kafka message. This is the catch-all for: malformed payloads, unrecognized RequestType values (which throw IllegalArgumentException from AbisRequestType.valueOf), NPEs, deserialization errors, or thread interruption during retry backoff. The exception propagates to the Kafka consumer which auto-retries with exponential backoff.

Thrown as an ApplicationException when a technical error occurs while processing the post-enrolment candidate completion response. After ABIS enrolment deduplication identifies potential duplicate candidates, the post-enrolment service processes completion responses for those candidates. If this processing fails, the exception propagates for Kafka retry.

DEAD CODE — defined but never thrown. The MDD-timeout feature is not wired in this codebase. SLA-breach events are handled separately by processSlaBreachEvent. The comment in source says 'keep till discussion'.
DEAD CODE — explicitly marked 'not in use' in source. Never thrown anywhere in active code.

Thrown as an ApplicationException when any non-ApplicationException runtime error occurs while processing an MFC (Manual Fraud Check) portal response. This is the catch-all for errors in duplicate-response checking, validation, helper-record fetching, portal-request preparation, candidate filtering, or PB2 routing within processMFCPortalResponse.

DEAD CODE — defined but never thrown. Its description is a copy-paste error ('Technical Error while processing MDD Packet Response'). The actually-thrown codes for consistency-check failure are: BIO_CONSISTENCY_CHECK_FAILED (business reject, applicant's own biometrics inconsistent) and SDK_CONSISTENCY_CHECK_PREPROCESSING_FAILED (technical error, from common-library TechnicalReasonCode).

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when the ABIS-MW quality response status is not SUCCESS (e.g. FAILURE, HOLD, or any unrecognized status). This is checked in isQualitySuccess() at BioDeDuplicationServiceImpl.java:1036. The packet is marked REJECTED and published to the bio stage completion topic. NOTE: This is different from the 9 BIO_QUALITY_* codes — those check per-modality thresholds on a SUCCESS-status response and are currently NOT acted upon due to a dead code branch (see critical finding #3).

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when the ABIS-MW enrolment or identify response status is neither 'SUCCESS' nor 'FAILURE' — e.g. 'HOLD', 'PARTIAL', an empty string, or any unexpected status value. Checked in isManualDedupRequired() at BioDeDuplicationServiceImpl.java:1174. The system will not guess what an unrecognized status means; the packet is rejected.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) in two scenarios: (1) In isManualDedupRequired() at line 1159 — when an ONLY_IDENTIFY ABIS response comes back SUCCESS, meaning the applicant's biometrics were found in the gallery as themselves, which for an update packet is treated as a failure (the master was not found as expected). (2) In processCREPolicyBatch0Response() at line 3360 — when CRE Policy Batch 0 explicitly rejected the applicant (and the applicant is not whitelisted/force-matched). The TODO comment at line 3359 indicates this is a catch-all for PB0 applicant rejections.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) in two scenarios: (1) In isCandidateManualDedupRequired() at line 1208 — when ABIS identify found NO matched candidates at all and no candidates are in-process, meaning the system could not find the resident's existing biometric identity in the ABIS gallery. (2) In processAutoDispositionResponseForNoMatchedCandidatesCase() at line 2765 — when all candidates have been filtered out during consistency/cross-match/PB1 processing and none remain. For update packets, this means the applicant's master identity could not be matched. For new enrolments (not update), validationError is null and the packet is APPROVED (no duplicates = success for new enrolment).

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when the ABIS-MW BIOUPDATE response status is not SUCCESS. The BIOUPDATE operation updates the resident's biometric template in the ABIS gallery. If ABIS-MW returns FAILURE or any non-SUCCESS status, the biometric template update has failed and the packet is rejected. The BIO_DEDUP_ABIS_BIO_UPDATE_REJECT_COUNTER metric is incremented.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when the consistency check determines the applicant's own biometrics are internally inconsistent. This means the resident's biometric captures across multiple attempts within the same enrolment session show significant variation — the same person's biometrics were not captured consistently. This could indicate device malfunction, operator error, or attempted fraud. Set in processConsistencyResponseToESB() at line 2440 when the consistency check response routes to ESB rejection instead of cross-match.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when CRE rejects the applicant but the match is NOT a confirmed True Duplicate (TD). This is the else branch of the TD check at line 3191: either (a) no matching EIDs were found in the reject-interceptor cache, or (b) the packet is an update case (not a new enrolment). If CRE provided explicit rejectReasonCodes, those codes replace this one on the packet (via prepareReasonCodeListForRejection + convertReasonCodesToValidationErrors at line 3200). NOTE: This code has NO numeric ID in BioDedupExceptionHelper — it is defined in the common-library BusinessReasonCode enum only.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when CRE PB1/PB2 rejects the applicant AND the reject-interceptor cache returned non-empty matching EIDs AND the packet is a new enrolment (not update). 'True Duplicate' means the applicant's biometrics match an existing Aadhaar holder confirmed as the same person (same EID). A DedupMatchingEidEvent is published to the reject-interceptor topic before recording the validation error. The packet is rejected to prevent duplicate Aadhaar issuance.

DEAD CODE as a thrown reason code — the enum constant is never thrown. The only runtime reference is at BioDeDuplicationServiceImpl.java:3579 in prepareReasonCodeListForRejection, which mines the description string from bioDedupReasonCodes.get(17041) to wrap CRE-supplied reject reason codes. The actual reject codes attached to the packet in that branch are the strings CRE supplied in rejectReasonCodes (converted to dynamic ValidationErrors), not this code.

DEAD CODE — defined but never thrown. The active code for applicant-side consistency failure is BIO_CONSISTENCY_CHECK_FAILED (from common-library BusinessReasonCode, no numeric ID). The active code for technical preprocessing failure of the consistency response is SDK_CONSISTENCY_CHECK_PREPROCESSING_FAILED (from common-library TechnicalReasonCode, no numeric ID).

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when, for an update packet, the ABIS gallery ID list built from UidOriginTracker records is empty — meaning there is no master biometric packet in the ABIS gallery for this UID. The resident's Aadhaar may have been issued without biometrics, or the biometric record was deleted. Set in ObjectTransformerServiceImpl.prepareAbisGalleryIdList at line 240; the packet is then routed to processRequestToEsbForRejection.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when an adult (age >= 5) new enrolment packet has the biometric bit OFF — meaning no biometrics (fingerprints/iris) were captured. Adults must have biometrics captured during enrolment. This is detected at processEnrolmentServiceBusResponse line 236-243 and the packet is routed to rejectBiometricAdultInvalidEnrolment at line 538. This is a packet preparation error at the enrolment client.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when a child (age < 5) packet contains biometric data (iris or finger count > 0). Children under 5 should not have biometrics captured — their enrolment is based on face-match data and a facial photo only. The presence of biometric data in a child's packet is invalid. Detected via childPacketContainsBiometrics at line 524 and routed to rejectBiometricChildInvalidCase at line 511.

Set as a ValidationError (terminal reject) when the ABIS-MW R-Verify response status is not SUCCESS. RVerify is a biometric verification service that checks whether the biometric data in the update packet matches the resident's existing biometric record in the ABIS gallery. A failure means the new biometric data does not match the stored biometrics, which could indicate wrong person, data corruption, or degraded biometrics.

The packet was rejected as an IVS (Identity Verification System) Healthy packet. IVS performs an identity verification check and the packet was flagged by IVS policy. This is a stage-level rejection from the SEDA pipeline.

A problem occurred while calling or validating the IVS (Identity Verification System) API. The IVS service was unreachable, returned an error, or the response failed validation. The packet is held pending a successful IVS check.

The packet was rejected because the fingerprint image quality score was below the acceptable threshold. Poor quality can result from dirty scanner glass, dry/wet fingers, incorrect finger placement, or device malfunction.

The packet was rejected because the fingerprint capture was not systematic — the captures were not taken in the correct sequence, or the capture device reported an inconsistency in the capture pattern.

The packet was rejected because the fingerprint liveness check failed. Liveness detection verifies the fingerprint is from a live human finger, not a fake/artificial fingerprint. A failure may indicate spoofing or sensor malfunction.

The packet was rejected because the iris image quality score was below the acceptable threshold. Poor quality can result from poor lighting, glasses/glare, closed eyes, incorrect distance from the scanner, or device malfunction.
The packet was rejected because the iris capture was not systematic — the captures were not taken in the correct sequence (left/right eye), or the device reported a capture pattern inconsistency.

The packet was rejected because the iris liveness check failed. Liveness detection verifies the iris is from a live human eye, not a printed image, contact lens with a fake iris pattern, or a prosthetic eye.

The packet was rejected because the face image quality score was below the acceptable threshold. Poor quality can result from poor lighting, blurred image, face not centered, accessories (glasses, mask, hat), or device malfunction.
The packet was rejected because the face capture was not systematic — the captures were not taken in the correct sequence or the device reported a capture pattern inconsistency.

The packet was rejected because the face liveness check failed. Liveness detection verifies the face is from a live human, not a photograph, video, or 3D mask. A failure may indicate spoofing or sensor malfunction.

rules.description: Policy/rule-based rejection rules evaluated by the rule engine. Each rule contains a condition and a resulting action. Only rules that result in the applicant being rejected are included.

CRE rejection rule in MDD_POLICY_BATCH_2. This rule fires when NOT (the applicant is whitelisted (previously reviewed and approved)); NOT (the applicant has a wrong biometric capture); NOT (at least one candidate has inconsistent biometrics); NOT (at least one candidate has a wrong capture); at least one candidate is a True Duplicate (confirmed same person); AND the number of face-duplicate candidates is exactly 0. The APPLICANT is REJECTED (the enrolment/update is denied). Candidates without Aadhaar are also REJECTED. Candidates that are SUSPENDED: CANDIDATES_WITH_AADHAAR.
rules.condition_description: NOT (the applicant is whitelisted (previously reviewed and approved)); NOT (the applicant has a wrong biometric capture); NOT (at least one candidate has inconsistent biometrics); NOT (at least one candidate has a wrong capture); at least one candidate is a True Duplicate (confirmed same person); AND the number of face-duplicate candidates is exactly 0

rules.description: CRE rejection rule in MDD_POLICY_BATCH_2. This rule fires when NOT (the applicant is whitelisted (previously reviewed and approved)); NOT (the applicant has a wrong biometric capture); NOT (at least one candidate has inconsistent biometrics); NOT (at least one candidate has a wrong capture); all candidates have matching face match (the applicant face photo matched the candidate face); AND there is more than 0 candidate(s) with Aadhaar; AND there is more than 0 non-NRC candidate(s) without Aadhaar. The APPLICANT is REJECTED (the enrolment/update is denied).

rules.description: CRE rejection rule in MDD_POLICY_BATCH_1. Reject reason code: RESIDENT_MAN_DEDUPE_REJECT_WL_DEMOMATCH_TD. This rule fires when the enrolment type is 'ENROLMENT' (New Enrolment); AND the applicant is whitelisted (previously reviewed and approved); all candidates have matching face match (the applicant face photo matched the candidate face); at least one True Duplicate candidate has an Aadhaar; AND there is more than 0 unique candidate(s); AND the number of unique candidates is at most 20; AND the number of whitelisted candidates that don't face-match is at most 0.
